_comment: Read by the detect-changes job of 5_builderpackage_agent-macos.yml through .github/actions/5_testintegration_detect-changes/detect_modules.py: a module is selected when ANY changed file of the pull request (three-dot diff) matches ANY of its `paths`. Positive globs only -- there is no `!` negation and no last-match-wins -- so a path listed here that the workflow's own `paths` excludes can never select anything: keep every entry inside that workflow's trigger. Comments live in these top-level `_comment*` keys only; every other key of a module is copied into the job matrix.
_comment_infra: Every module that names a daemon repeats the plumbing that can change any suite's result: the package workflow that builds the agent under test, the integration workflow, this file, the interpreter version, the package hand-off action, and the build configuration every binary goes through (src/Makefile, src/CMakeLists.txt, src/cmake/**, src/external/CMakeLists.txt, src/deps.lock.mk), plus tests/integration/conftest.py and pytest.ini.
_comment_core: Every agent daemon links libwazuh (src/shared/**) and libconfig (src/config/CMakeLists.txt, config.c/config.h dispatch every section), so each daemon module lists them next to the daemon's own tree, its config readers and the first-party libraries it links directly (target_link_libraries of the daemon's CMakeLists.txt). Left out on purpose: wazuh_modulesd_lib, which agentd, logcollector and execd also link (it would make every suite depend on every module), and the server headers libwazuh includes (src/os_auth/include, src/wazuh_db/include) -- a break there fails the package build, which those paths do fire.
_comment_modulesd: aws, github, office365, sca and syscollector run inside wazuh-modulesd: they add its host (src/wazuh_modules/CMakeLists.txt, include/**, main.c, wmodules.c, wmcom.c, wm_exec.c, wm_sendmsg.c, src/config/src/wmodules-config.c) to their own shim and reader.
_comment_fim: syscheckd links rootcheck, dbsync, agent_sync_protocol, schema_validator and fimdb (src/syscheckd/CMakeLists.txt).
